ALG-H5-01.solved: Infinitely many solutions means the second equation is a multiple of the first. -15y = 3(-5y), so the factor is 3: a = 9, b = 3(12) = 36. a + b = 45.
ALG-H5-01.note: 36 = b alone, 21 = 9 + 12 (forgetting to scale b). One idea (proportionality of coefficients); routine module-1 fare.

ALG-H5-02.solved: 240 + 12n < 27n  ->  240 < 15n  ->  n > 16, so the least integer is 17.
ALG-H5-02.note: 16 is the strict-vs-nonstrict boundary trap and is the option most students will land on. Same shape as 07, 15 and 18 (see batch note on 18).

ALG-H5-03.note: 29 is the sign-flipped slope. Pure slope-then-substitute; one idea.

ALG-H5-04.solved: RHS must be non-negative, so x >= 4. Case x >= 10: x - 10 = 2x - 8 gives x = -2, rejected. Case x < 10: 10 - x = 2x - 8 gives 3x = 18, x = 6, which satisfies x >= 4. So x = 6.
ALG-H5-04.note: -2 is the genuine extraneous root and 18 comes from |x-10| = 2x - 8 mishandled as x - 10 = -(2x - 8). Best distractor set in the batch. Still one idea (case split plus domain check), which is a standard medium.

ALG-H5-05.note: 15 is 25% of 60 and 21 is the total acid, both reachable by grabbing the wrong quantity. 24 I could not trace to a wrong path - mildly weak. Note the mixture wording asks for the 55% amount, not the 25% amount (40), and 40 is not offered, which removes the most common error.

ALG-H5-06.solved: 5x - 8 > 17 gives x > 5; 2x + 1 < 41 gives x < 20. Greatest integer strictly below 20 is 19.
ALG-H5-06.note: 20 is the non-strict trap. Two inequalities but they do not interact - only the upper one is used, so the 'compound' framing is decoration.

ALG-H5-07.solved: 8400 - 120t < 5600 + 200t  ->  2800 < 320t  ->  t > 8.75, so the first whole year is 9.
ALG-H5-07.note: 8 is the floor-instead-of-ceiling trap. Structurally identical to 02.

ALG-H5-08.note: 39 = 3a, 7 = a - 6. Two-step substitution; this is a module-1 easy.

ALG-H5-09.note: 51 is the forgot-the-minus-8 option and will catch people. Recognising the multiple is one idea, not two.

ALG-H5-10.solved: 4x + 10y = 15  ->  y = -(2/5)x + 3/2, slope -2/5. Perpendicular slope 5/2. Through (10, -1): y = -1 + (5/2)(x - 10) = (5/2)x - 26. y-intercept -26.
ALG-H5-10.note: 24 is the sign error on the intercept, 3 is the intercept of the ORIGINAL line (3/2 rounded up - a bit loose). Longish but routine: rearrange, negative reciprocal, point-slope.

ALG-H5-11.solved: First 8 minutes: 8(12) = 96 pages. Remaining 396 - 96 = 300 pages at 20/min = 15 minutes. Total 8 + 15 = 23.
ALG-H5-11.note: 15 is the forgot-to-add-the-first-8-minutes answer and 33 = 396/12 (single rate). Both are real student paths.

ALG-H5-12.solved: 15x - 10 + a = bx + 6. No solution requires equal x-coefficients with unequal constants, so b = 15 (and a != 16).
ALG-H5-12.note: 16 is the value of a that would instead give infinitely many solutions - a well-chosen distractor. Small logical looseness in the stem: with b = 15 the equation has no solution only when a != 16, and a is never constrained; the question asks only for b so the answer survives, but a picky student sees the gap.

ALG-H5-13.note: 160 is the jacket's ORIGINAL price - the single most likely miss, since the last step is easy to skip. 142 = 102 + 40 (applying the 40 to the reduced price).

ALG-H5-14.solved: s + L = 54 and 3s = L + 14. Substituting L = 54 - s: 3s = 68 - s  ->  s = 17, L = 37.
ALG-H5-14.note: 51 = 3(17) (reporting 3s), 68 is the intermediate. Standard two-equation word problem.

ALG-H5-15.solved: 180 + 45d <= 2300  ->  45d <= 2120  ->  d <= 47.11, so at most 47 days; but the rental must be a whole number of weeks, so d must be a multiple of 7. The largest multiple of 7 at or below 47 is 42.
ALG-H5-15.note: One of only two genuinely hard items here: the budget inequality and the discrete whole-weeks constraint actually interact, and the continuous answer 47 is offered as the trap. 6 is the answer in weeks (the stem asks for days) - fair but a second live trap.

ALG-H5-16.solved: Translating up 8 gives y = -4x + 28. Setting y = 0: x = 7.
ALG-H5-16.note: 5 is the original x-intercept, 3 is the down-8 translation. Two mechanical steps, no interaction.

ALG-H5-17.solved: w + k = 80 and 20w + 35k = 2020. Substituting: 1600 + 15k = 2020  ->  k = 28 weekend hours.
ALG-H5-17.note: 52 (the weekday hours) is NOT offered, which removes the classic answered-the-other-variable trap and makes this easier than it should be. 58 and 37 I could not trace to clean wrong paths.

ALG-H5-18.note: 26 is the round-up trap and 33 = 500/15 (ignoring the 40-item constraint). Nearest miss on hard: it needs substitution plus a floor, but only one constraint does real work after substitution. Batch note: 02, 06, 07, 15, 18 and 24 are all 'solve a linear inequality, then take the boundary integer' - six of 24 items on one template, with the boundary option planted each time. A student who learns 'do not round the way it feels' gets a quarter of the batch.

ALG-H5-19.note: 11 is exactly the solve-3x-7=26-and-stop answer, which is the intended miss; 39 = 3a. Good distractors, but the item is one substitution.

ALG-H5-20.solved: Let pears = 4k, apples = 7k. Then 4k/(7k + 12) = 4/9  ->  36k = 28k + 48  ->  k = 6, so apples before = 7(6) = 42.
ALG-H5-20.note: 24 = pears, 54 = apples after, 6 = k. Every wrong option is a real intermediate value. Solid item; the pears staying fixed is the only insight, so medium rather than hard.

ALG-H5-21.solved: |a - 480| <= 12 gives a in [468, 492]; |b - 450| <= 14 gives b in [436, 464]. a - b is greatest at a max and b min: 492 - 436 = 56.
ALG-H5-21.note: The second genuinely hard item: two absolute-value inequalities have to be converted to intervals AND the optimisation has to pair the max of one with the MIN of the other. 30 (centre difference) and 28 (12 + 14 applied to the wrong endpoints) are exactly the two ways to miss it.

ALG-H5-23.note: 7 is the x-value the stem deliberately does not ask for, and it is offered. Clean two-step.

ALG-H5-24.note: -8 is the failed-to-divide step, 1 is the sign flip. Same inequality-boundary template as 02/06/07/15/18.
